title: NeoChain WMS
org: NeoChain Co. — digital transformation for manufacturing SMEs
summary: A Wenzhou auto-parts factory ran on paper checklists; the generic ERP did not fit how goods actually moved. After a visit to the floor I built a warehouse system in two halves: a PDA app for line workers and a web admin for line managers.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Co-founder / Full-Stack — PRD, architecture, PDA app, admin portal

facts.label: Scope
facts.value: 7 floor workflows · barcode PDA · one admin overview

sections.heading: The problem
paragraphs: Paper checklists mean data gaps: no one knows what is on the shelf until someone walks over. Off-the-shelf ERPs model a different factory, so workers route around them and the paper comes back.

sections.heading: PDA for the floor
paragraphs: Seven workflows — receiving, put-away, picking, line inbound, production closing, line packing, sales outbound — each a state machine on a handheld scanner. Every step is confirmed before the next; you cannot skip one or misconfirm a package in a noisy, rushed handoff.

image.alt: PDA home screen with seven workflow tiles and pending counts

sections.heading: Admin for line managers
paragraphs: One overview: frames waiting for put-away, line WIP utilisation, goods waiting for QC, today's yield; inbound and outbound orders with progress; the production trend; line tasks; an anomaly monitor. Master data lives here too.
